b1c8ec8cbd.q: How did Schupan Sons grow from a five-person scrapyard in Kalamazoo, Michigan to 600 employees across 18 locations?
b1c8ec8cbd.a: Schupan Sons was started by Jordan's grandfather as a five-person scrapyard in Kalamazoo, Michigan, primarily to support his family after his death. Under his father Mark's 53-year leadership, the company grew by listening to the market and customers. They expanded from industrial accounts into the beverage deposit space, aluminum EBC processing and trading, metal service centers selling new materials, and precision machining and fabrication work across multiple states. The company now operates 18 locations with 600 employees.

c1ac39d4eb.q: What was Jordan Schupan's career path before joining Schupan Sons as CEO in 2017?
c1ac39d4eb.a: Jordan worked in software startups at the Series A and B stage, where one company went public and another was acquired. He started in sales roles in fast-paced, venture-backed growth environments where job security depended quarter-to-quarter on sales numbers. In 2016, after earning money from selling enterprise software licenses, he traveled around the world for a few months. He was also close to joining Snowflake at the time, but decided to pursue opportunities in the family business instead.

10d9c6415c.q: What role did Tom Emerick play in bringing Jordan Schupan back to the family business?

66c0f149c6.q: How did Schupan Sons expand from a Midwest processor to a national aluminum trader?
66c0f149c6.a: When Jordan joined in January 2017, Schupan Sons was primarily a Midwest processor. He worked with Andy McKee, who became a great partner in building out the trading business. Together they had opportunities to buy metal from more places beyond the Midwest, expanding the company's reach nationally. Jordan handled West Coast buying operations and spent considerable time in Michigan, while Andy expanded sourcing from additional regions, transforming the company from regional to national scope.

a067eefb4a.q: What motivated Jordan Schupan to leave the software startup world and return to Schupan Sons?
a067eefb4a.a: After gaining independence and financial success in 2016, Jordan reflected on what truly motivated him long-term. He realized the family business had been around almost 50 years with an incredible brand, and it was how he and his father had always connected since childhood. He worried that if something happened and he had not taken the opportunity to work with his father, he would regret it. He also recognized the potential impact of being part of a private company with only a few owners, where business success directly benefits employees, and the stability of long-term shareholders with great people.
